findings.summary: SDL and Dawn repeated the same startup loop that makes renderer passes current after synchronizing render textures. Both startup paths now reuse sync_renderer_passes(), keeping pass allocation and refresh ordering in one backend-local implementation.

Static file textures eagerly decoded PNG dimensions even when the source never observed width or height. The compiler now retains source metadata and reads the PNG header only when a dimension member is reached.

Tuple callback indices were emitted as native locals even though each index is fixed by the statically unrolled tuple position. Binding them as compile-time values removes dead generated locals and lets downstream numeric lowering fold the index directly.

Returned-struct storage is reference-backed only when that return type is stored in an Array, Map, Set, or Record in the reached program, preserving value semantics for pure builders while giving stored game records stable identity.

Live SDL key events and deterministic keyboard replay duplicated DOM event construction and callback selection. Both now use dispatch_platform_keyboard_event(), so key mapping and down/up routing have one implementation.
File-backed and render-target-backed grid atlases duplicated the frame partition. Both now call populate_grid_sprite_atlas_frames(), preventing the two createGridSpriteAtlas paths from drifting.

SpriteRenderTextureRecord carried a destroyed flag that no writer or reader used because reached destroy calls deliberately retain engine-owned GPU resources. Removing it keeps the runtime record aligned with its actual state.

Continuation persistence initially recognized every later assignment to a post-start local as another declaration and could emit invalid static assignments. Persistence now consumes each storage name at its first declaration, with regressions covering later top-level writes and existing post-start destructuring.

The three frame-loop shapes repeated RAF timestamp capture and callback dispatch. They now share run_animation_frame_callbacks(), and the relocated CaptureGate contract once again documents the class it governs.

Compiler scope bindings and frame-callback signature literals were duplicated across the compiler, expression context, and closure records. VariableBinding and FrameCallbackSignature now provide one typed definition.

Dawn's startup-only surface configuration would have been copied into resize handling. configure_dawn_surface() now owns both paths, and resize_dawn_surface() guards unchanged extents before reconfiguration.

Named frame callback adapters must preserve the browser-supplied delta or timestamp even when the JavaScript callback ignores it. Marking the generated adapter parameter [[maybe_unused]] keeps that single signature path warning-clean without branching on callback arity.
